BERT: 1. achieves new state of the-art results on eleven natural lan guage processing tasks, 2. is conceptually simple (it uses bidirectional transformers to learn contextual repre sentations), 3. can be fine tuned for any task without task specific architecture changes, and 4. is pre trained from a combination of unsupervised and supervised data.

BERT: 1. obtains new state of art results on eleven NLP tasks by simply being fine tuned, 2. is conceptually simple, 3. can be scaled to much larger models than have been previously considered, and 4. can be pre trained from scratch without task specific supervision data.

(1) deep bidirectional representations can be pre trained on unlabeled text by predicting both the forward and backward words in a sentence (2) these bidirectional representations are useful for a wide array of downstream tasks, such as textual entailment and question answering, with just a small fine tuning phase, and (3) BERT outperforms current state of the art representations on eleven tasks.

deep bidirectional language representations can be pre trained to achieve state of the art in a wide range of task, with just one change in the architecture: replacing the stack of unidirectional LSTMs with a stack of bidirectional LSTMs.
